note: Adapted from Maiti 2006; original in English; the archive.org scan is the extracted text of the publisher's PDF (good OCR; decimal points were converted to spaces, e.g. "1 54-1 76" is 1.54—1.76), and the measurements have been restored according to the original table. In Table 12 the head height row is a single value that does not correspond to the three columns, and it is not recorded.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head rectangular-oval, longer than wide, sides nearly parallel, narrowing anteriorly and posteriorly from the middle, the anterior part distinctly paler; fontanelle small, its opening with a chitinous ring, situated at the posterior margin of the postclypeus; antennae 16-segmented; anterior margin of the pronotum convex with a deep median notch. Alate head nearly circular, ocelli small, forewing scale almost twice as long as the hindwing scale, wing membrane hairy. It differs from C. acinaciformis raffrayi in that the latter has smaller ocelli in the alate (0.11—0.16 mm, 0.14—0.18 mm in the nominotypical subspecies), a narrower maximum postmentum width in the soldier (0.42 mm, 0.50 mm in the nominotypical subspecies) and a wider anterior margin of the head (0.84—0.99 mm, 0.80—0.90 mm in the nominotypical subspecies).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head, pronotum and wing scales light brown, the vertex darker brown; antennae and legs pale yellow, wing veins brown. Head and pronotum moderately hairy, wings and abdomen densely hairy. Head nearly circular, slightly arched dorsally, posterolateral margins slightly rounded; compound eyes medium-sized, rather variable; postclypeus about one quarter as long as wide; antennae 17—21-segmented, segments 2—4 variable; ocelli small (0.14—0.18 mm), elongate. Pronotum narrower than the head, anterior margin weakly incurved with a weak median notch, anterolateral corners narrowly rounded, posterior margin with a deep median concavity. Forewing scale very large, almost twice as long as the hindwing scale; costa and radial sector distinct, the other veins weak; wing membrane hairy. Measurements (mm): body length with wings 11.50—14.25; body length without wings 6.00—7.50; head length to the lateral base of the mandible 0.90—0.95; head width including the eyes 1.28—1.35; maximum eye diameter 0.33—0.44; maximum ocellus diameter 0.14—0.18; pronotum length 0.69—0.80, width 1.13—1.32; forewing length 8.60—11.00; antennae 17—20-segmented.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head straw yellow, sparsely hairy; antennae, pronotum and legs paler. Head rectangular-oval, slightly longer than wide, sides nearly parallel, gradually narrowing anteriorly and posteriorly from the middle; fontanelle small, its opening with a chitinous ring, situated almost at the posterior margin of the postclypeus; eyes and ocelli absent. Antennae 16-segmented, segments 2 and 3 nearly equal in length, or segment 3 slightly smaller than segment 2, segment 4 longer than segment 3; postclypeus distinct; labrum nearly triangular, the tip strongly recurved and transparent. Postmentum rod-like, widest in the anterior quarter, narrowest in the posterior quarter; pronotum wider than long, anterior margin convex but with a deep median notch, posterior margin weakly concave at the middle. Measurements (mm): head length to the lateral base of the mandible 1.54—1.76; maximum head width 1.21—1.35; anterior head width 0.80—0.90; mandible length 1.14; postmentum midlength 1.00, maximum width 0.50, waist width 0.23—0.29; pronotum length 0.46—0.57, width 0.84—1.02; antennae 15—17-segmented.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Maiti (2006) gives the measurements of the alate and the soldier in Tables 4 and 12 respectively and treats raffrayi as a subspecies of this species, with the subspecies measurements in Tables 7 and 26. The original gives a single value, 0.88 mm, for head height in the soldier, which cannot be matched to the other two columns of the same table, and it is not recorded.
